group: Valid walk with validation (JSON input, validate = true)

cases.expected: ValidationResult with isSuccess() == true and no ValidationMessage entries
cases.description: A well‑formed JSON document is supplied, the format is JSON and validation is requested. The method should deserialize the string and invoke walkAtNodeInternal with validation enabled, returning a successful ValidationResult.

group: Valid walk without validation (JSON input, validate = false)

cases.expected: ValidationResult with isSuccess() == true (or at least no validation errors) – the walk should complete even though validation is disabled
cases.description: Even when validation is turned off, walk should still deserialize the input and walk the schema tree without performing validation checks.
The JSON string is syntactically incorrect; deserialize should throw a JsonProcessingException which propagates out of walk.

group: Null input string – handling of null payload

cases.expected: throws NullPointerException or IllegalArgumentException (depending on deserialize implementation)
cases.description: Passing a null input string should cause deserialize to reject the argument; the test verifies that the appropriate exception is thrown.

group: YAML input format – successful deserialization and validation

cases.expected: ValidationResult with isSuccess() == true and no ValidationMessage entries
cases.description: A correct YAML document is supplied; deserialize should use YamlMapperFactory and produce a JsonNode that can be walked and validated successfully.

group: Unsupported InputFormat – fallback or error handling

cases.expected: throws IllegalArgumentException (or a custom exception) because inputFormat is null/unsupported
cases.description: When the inputFormat argument is null or not recognized, deserialize should reject the call, causing walk to throw an exception.

group: Invalid JSON input – deserialization failure with validation disabled

cases.description: Even when validation is disabled, the method must first deserialize the payload. An ill‑formed JSON string should cause a JsonProcessingException to be propagated.
A malformed YAML document should trigger a deserialization error regardless of the validate flag.

cases.expected: throws com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonProcessingException (or a subclass) because an empty string is not valid JSON
cases.description: An empty payload cannot be parsed into a JsonNode; the method should surface the parsing exception.

cases.expected: throws com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonProcessingException (or a subclass) because whitespace alone is not a valid JSON document
cases.description: Even though the string contains only whitespace, Jackson treats it as invalid JSON and throws an exception.

cases.expected: throws NullPointerException (or IllegalArgumentException) because executionContext is required
cases.description: The method expects a non‑null ExecutionContext; passing null should result in an immediate exception before deserialization.

group: Valid YAML input without validation (validate = false)

cases.expected: ValidationResult with isSuccess() == true (no ValidationMessage entries) – validation is skipped but walk completes
cases.description: When validation is disabled, walk should still deserialize the YAML and traverse the schema tree without producing validation messages.

group: Valid JSON literal null input – walk succeeds

cases.expected: ValidationResult with isSuccess() == true (or no ValidationMessage entries) – the JSON literal null is deserialized to a NullNode and walked without errors
cases.description: A JSON document that is the literal `null` should be handled gracefully; deserialization yields a NullNode which the walk algorithm can process.

group: Valid JSON array input – walk succeeds

cases.expected: ValidationResult with isSuccess() == true (no ValidationMessage entries) – array nodes are supported and should not cause errors in a permissive schema
cases.description: Ensures that the walk method correctly handles a root JSON array after successful deserialization.

group: Valid JSON number input – walk succeeds

cases.expected: ValidationResult with isSuccess() == true (no ValidationMessage entries) – numeric root nodes are deserialized to NumericNode and walked without issues
cases.description: Verifies that a simple numeric JSON document is processed correctly by walk.

group: Valid JSON empty object – walk succeeds

cases.expected: ValidationResult with isSuccess() == true (no ValidationMessage entries) – an empty object should be accepted by a schema that does not require properties
cases.description: Confirms that a minimal valid JSON object does not cause unexpected validation failures.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or a subclass) because the supplied InputFormat is not supported by JsonSchema.deserialize
cases.description: Passing a valid InputFormat enum constant that the library does not handle (e.g., XML) should cause deserialize to reject the request and the walk method to throw an IllegalArgumentException.
